# Marshall Elliott

## Overview

- **Age:** About fifty years old during Anne's first year of teaching.  <sub>[v2 c9 P22](../source/v02-c09.md#nw-v02-c09-p0022)</sub>
- **Gender:** Male  <sub>[v2 c9 P0](../source/v02-c09.md#nw-v02-c09-p0000)</sub>
- **Status:** Married  <sub>[v5 c32 P12](../source/v05-c32.md#nw-v05-c32-p0012), [v5 c35 P0](../source/v05-c35.md#nw-v05-c35-p0000)</sub>
- **Origin:** Avonlea / Glen St. Mary area  <sub>[v2 c9 P22](../source/v02-c09.md#nw-v02-c09-p0022), [v4 c9 P33](../source/v04-c09.md#nw-v04-c09-p0033)</sub>
- **Role:** Farmer  <sub>[v2 c9 P0](../source/v02-c09.md#nw-v02-c09-p0000), [v4 c9 P32](../source/v04-c09.md#nw-v04-c09-p0032)</sub>

## Appearance

Marshall Elliott is a tall, broad-shouldered man with a strong, clean-shaven chin and frank gray eyes. For fifteen years, due to a political vow, he wore a river of crinkly brown beard reaching nearly to his knees and a corresponding cascade of thick, wavy brown hair down his back, giving him the look of a dime museum freak or a Viking. After shaving his beard and cutting his hair, he was revealed as a handsome, well-featured man with a mane of red hair.

_Sources: [v2 c9 P0](../source/v02-c09.md#nw-v02-c09-p0000), [v4 c9 P13](../source/v04-c09.md#nw-v04-c09-p0013), [v4 c9 P32](../source/v04-c09.md#nw-v04-c09-p0032), [v4 c9 P35](../source/v04-c09.md#nw-v04-c09-p0035), [v4 c35 P28](../source/v04-c35.md#nw-v04-c35-p0028), [v5 c16 P28](../source/v05-c16.md#nw-v05-c16-p0028)_

## Personality

Marshall Elliott is a passionate, outspoken, and stubborner-than-average man with an intense devotion to political causes. Despite his eccentricities and fierce temper, he is a witty, intelligent, and well-read companion who enjoys telling stories and engaging in spirited arguments. He possesses a strong sense of honor, refusing to break his word once given. He is also capable of great generosity and kindness, being deeply moved to anger by any mistreatment of children.

_Sources: [v2 c9 P0](../source/v02-c09.md#nw-v02-c09-p0000), [v4 c9 P32](../source/v04-c09.md#nw-v04-c09-p0032), [v4 c9 P36](../source/v04-c09.md#nw-v04-c09-p0036), [v4 c11 P31](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0031), [v4 c16 P7](../source/v04-c16.md#nw-v04-c16-p0007), [v5 c13 P20](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0020), [v5 c16 P55](../source/v05-c16.md#nw-v05-c16-p0055), [v5 c16 P79](../source/v05-c16.md#nw-v05-c16-p0079)_

## History

Marshall Elliott was an ardent Liberal who vowed during a fierce campaign that he would not cut his hair or shave his beard until the Liberal party returned to power. As the Conservatives remained in office for fifteen years, he grew an extraordinarily long hair and beard that earned him a reputation as an eccentric. When the Liberals finally won a general election years later, he immediately went to a barber at midnight to be shaved and groomed. Having been a long-time suitor and former fiancé of Ellen West in his youth, he resumed his courtship after his years of isolation and eventually married her, moving to her home at the West farm. Known for his boisterous humor and fiery temper, he nevertheless formed warm friendships with neighbours like Captain Jim, Anne, and Gilbert, and fiercely defended those he cared for.

_Sources: [v4 c9 P33](../source/v04-c09.md#nw-v04-c09-p0033), [v4 c35 P28](../source/v04-c35.md#nw-v04-c35-p0028), [v4 c35 P29](../source/v04-c35.md#nw-v04-c35-p0029), [v4 c37 P9](../source/v04-c37.md#nw-v04-c37-p0009), [v5 c15 P29](../source/v05-c15.md#nw-v05-c15-p0029), [v5 c32 P12](../source/v05-c32.md#nw-v05-c32-p0012), [v5 c35 P2](../source/v05-c35.md#nw-v05-c35-p0002)_

## Background by volume

- Born into the Elliott family of Avonlea and Glen St. Mary  <sub>[v2 c9 P22](../source/v02-c09.md#nw-v02-c09-p0022), [v4 c9 P33](../source/v04-c09.md#nw-v04-c09-p0033)</sub>
- Courted Ellen West in his youth, but jilted her after a pique-driven quarrel and hastily married Hester Reese, who later died  <sub>[v5 c15 P29](../source/v05-c15.md#nw-v05-c15-p0029), [v5 c15 P30](../source/v05-c15.md#nw-v05-c15-p0030), [v5 c21 P0](../source/v05-c21.md#nw-v05-c21-p0000)</sub>
- Vowed during a bitter election campaign fifteen years prior not to shave or cut his hair until the Liberals came into power  <sub>[v4 c9 P33](../source/v04-c09.md#nw-v04-c09-p0033)</sub>

## Quotes

> Come into your shop and do the best job you ever did in your life, Gus. The Liberals are in and you’re going to barber a good Grit before the sun rises.  <sub>[v4 c35 P29](../source/v04-c35.md#nw-v04-c35-p0029)</sub>

> I made a fool of myself and I’m sorry. Man can’t say fairer. Forget and forgive. Shake hands, girl—shake hands.  <sub>[v5 c16 P59](../source/v05-c16.md#nw-v05-c16-p0059)</sub>

> I used to be a great hand for the ladies, but I’ve got over it.  <sub>[v4 c9 P32](../source/v04-c09.md#nw-v04-c09-p0032)</sub>
